assets.name: rad_emo_dataset_overview
assets.prompt:
Use case: scientific-educational
Asset type: landscape raster illustration for a scientific dataset repository, suitable for a Zenodo description or GitHub landing page.
Primary request: A polished, accurate visual overview of RAD-EMO, a multimodal laboratory dataset of object carriage and reported affect.
Style: restrained editorial scientific illustration, clear flat shapes with subtle depth, white background, navy typography, teal and muted orange accents, generous whitespace, exceptionally readable text. Wide 3:2 composition, high resolution.
Layout: top title "RAD-EMO"; subtitle "Object carriage and reported affect". Under it three compact statistic badges reading exactly "15 participants", "114 recordings", "38 conditions". Central non-identifiable human silhouette in a minimal abstract laboratory recording space, surrounded by four equally weighted sensor illustrations: a conventional camera labelled "RGB images"; a second imaging camera with a plainly illustrative warm-colour silhouette tile labelled "Thermal images"; a compact radar board with abstract wave arcs labelled "mmWave radar"; a small fingertip pulse sensor labelled "Pulse records". Arrange these as four distinct channels connecting to a lower folder labelled "Recording-level data". A small final line at the bottom reads "Images • Radar measurements • Annotations • Metadata".
Constraints: This is a conceptual dataset illustration, not a depiction of the actual lab or a captured participant. Put the small, readable caption "Conceptual illustration" in the bottom right. Keep all visual sensor outputs schematic, without fabricated plots, measured values, faces, identities or claimed sensor positioning. No timelines, no fps number, no synchronisation claims, no model performance, no neural networks, no paper references, no associated-study wording, no companion package, no dangerousness labels. Do not invent hardware brands or architecture. No additional text beyond the specified title, subtitle, badges, four channel labels, folder label, final line and small caption.
assets.edit_prompt: Edit this RAD-EMO dataset overview illustration. Remove the briefcase/bag from the central human silhouette and from BOTH the RGB sample tile and the thermal sample tile. All three depictions must have empty hands, with relaxed arms. Also replace the orange ECG-like waveform in the Pulse records tile with a simple abstract pulse-sensor icon; no measured-looking graph is needed. Preserve the entire layout, every text label verbatim, the four sensor channels, colour palette, title, badges and small Conceptual illustration caption. Do not change any other elements. The figure illustrates a laboratory dataset with phone and replica-knife carriage; no briefcase should appear. Keep a polished scientific illustration, no new text or sensor measurements.

assets.name: rad_emo_recording_conditions
assets.prompt:
Use case: scientific-educational
Asset type: landscape raster infographic explaining the contents of the RAD-EMO laboratory dataset; a companion figure to its repository description.
Primary request: A clear, attractive guide to the recording conditions and reported-affect labels, independent of any model or publication.
Style: match a restrained scientific editorial design: white background, navy headings, teal and muted orange accents, softly shaded flat illustrations, high-quality typography, generous whitespace. Wide 3:2 composition, high resolution.
Exact title: "RAD-EMO recording conditions".
Layout: four horizontal sections with clear spacing.
Section 1 heading "Object carriage". Four illustrated cards, labelled exactly "No object", "Phone", "Replica knife", "Phone + replica knife". Use generic faceless human silhouettes and clear object icons. The replica knife should be a simple blunt training prop, never used against anyone.
Section 2 heading "Activity". Two cards labelled "Still" and "Walking", with simple faceless silhouettes.
Section 3 heading "Placement". Two cards labelled "Open" and "Concealed". Show visible held objects versus a clothing pocket with a dotted object outline used as a schematic explanatory convention. Keep this categorical, not a detector localisation example.
Section 4 heading "Reported affect". Three clearly separate labelled, unfilled horizontal scales reading "Valence", "Arousal", "Dominance", each with endpoints "0" and "9". They are scale definitions, not observations; do not add participant scores, plotted dots or curves.
Footer line exactly "15 participants · 114 recordings · 38 protocol conditions". Bottom-right small readable caption "Conceptual illustration".
Constraints: Do not draw a full factorial experimental design or imply every pictured factor combination was collected. No facial identities, no realistic data samples, no fps, no synchronisation, no neural networks, no classifiers or results, no study or companion references, no threat/dangerousness labels, no extra numerical claims.
